caption: Three separate SafeMesh apps run on three HarmonyOS (API 24) emulators. A local test link stands in for the NearLink radio: A and B are in range, C is out of range.
Each phone joins the relay in its role. Recipients have no Send button: verified alerts are stored and relayed automatically.
A is an authenticated exercise issuer. A separate signing service holds the private key; the phone only receives the signed alert and verifies it before saving.
A publishes an English exercise alert: ECDSA P-256 signature, critical priority, valid for one hour.
B verifies the signature on the device, saves the alert, returns an app-level ACK and shows a banner. C is out of range and has nothing yet.
A leaves the area and B meets C, with no internet and no cellular network. C receives the alert from B at hop 2, although A and C were never connected.
A forged copy is injected (text changed after signing). C rejects it: no ACK, not stored, not forwarded.
Offline map: 40 State Fire Service (PSP) protective points in central Kraków ship inside the app. Address search works without Polish diacritics.
The NearLink adapter (NearLink Kit) is built in. Emulators have no radio and report that; a physical phone-to-phone NearLink test is next.
